title: Sequential Toolchain Composer — personal PRD sketch
content:
Quick brain-dump: an idea for a tiny product/feature that lets devs assemble short, sequential toolchains (call LLM -> run a small code transform -> call a reranker / embedder) with explicit cost and latency estimates, and a runtime that can schedule steps on different deployment tiers (hosted/dedicated/private).

Problem space
- Many teams end up wiring together 2–4 discrete steps around an LLM call (e.g., parse user, normalize, call model, run a deterministic post-process, call search) but lack an easy UI to describe sequence + runtime constraints.
- Ops/PMs want visibility: which steps run on private infra vs hosted, and estimated cost per request.
- Currently folks write fragile glue: serverless functions, ad-hoc queues, or heavyweight pipelines.

Proposed feature: Sequential Toolchain Composer (STC) — sketch
- Lightweight composer UI (and a YAML/JSON definition) representing an ordered list of steps. Steps are small, typed actions: prompt->LLM, run-webhook, run-js-snippet (sandbox), embed->search, rerank, store-to-kv, branching by predicate.
- Each step declares resource preferences: prefer_private | prefer_dedicated | prefer_hosted, max_latency_ms, cost_hint (low/med/high).
- Composer surfaces estimated per-step cost and latency (based on model profiles + historical execution timings).
- Runtime executes steps with a scheduler that can: pipeline steps in the same pod when possible, offload heavy steps to dedicated pools, or fallback to hosted variants if capacity constrained.
- Support simple branching and retries but keep UX focused on linear flows (not full DAG orchestration) so it's approachable for product teams.

User stories (examples)
- As a product engineer, I want to compose an onramp flow: user input -> small instruction-tuned model (hosted) -> lightweight JS sanitizer (edge) -> embed + semantic search (dedicated) -> rerank (hosted fallback) so I can iterate quickly without infra changes.
- As an SRE, I want step-level telemetry and per-step error budgets so we can alert on which step is failing.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to export a toolchain definition to a customer’s private deployment with minimal changes.

Success metrics (initial)
- 30% reduction in time-to-prototype multi-step LLM features (measured by internal experiments).
- 20% fewer ad-hoc lambda glue functions used across sample apps (tracked via inventory).
- Users can toggle step routing (hosted/dedicated/private) and see cost delta immediately.

MVP scope (keep tight)
- UI sketch + saveable JSON definition for linear sequences up to 6 steps.
- Step types: LLM call, JS sandbox (restricted), HTTP webhook, embed+search, rerank.
- Scheduler: naive sequential executor with routing hints respected; no complex DAGs, limited branching (if/else on step result).
- Instrumentation: per-step latency/cost estimate and logs surfaced in Console -> Route view.

Nice-to-haves (post-MVP)
- Step-level caching/prefix-KV hints, automatic batching of identical LLM steps across concurrent requests.
- A small templating gallery (starter toolchains) for common use-cases: conversational memory injectors, semantic FAQ, code assist chains.
- Visual diffing & rollout: can A/B two toolchains for a route.

Constraints & risks
- Security: running user-provided JS/snippets is risky. Need sandboxing + limited syscall/HTTP egress. Consider WASM sandbox + vetting.
- Complexity drift: if we allow full DAGs this becomes a workflow product; intentionally limit scope.
- Cost estimation accuracy: need baseline models and sampling to produce credible estimates; bad estimates will erode trust.

Implementation notes / rough tech approach
- Toolchain definition = small JSON schema. Keep step contract typed: input_type, output_type, required_metadata.
- Scheduler picks placement by step preference + runtime capacity; fallback chain: preferred -> compatible -> hosted. Keep greedy algorithm in MVP.
- Meter per-step token usage and compute; surface sample billing calc in Console.
- JS sandbox executes in a pinned runtime container with strict timeouts (50–200ms depending on step SLA). Consider using Wasmtime + WASI for safety.

Open questions / parking lot
- Should toolchains be versioned independently from models? (prob yes)
- Authorization model: who can create toolchains for a route? RBAC mapping to org roles.
- UI: full drag-drop vs simple ordered list editor? Start simple list editor.
- How to test e2e? Need a lightweight harness that can replay traffic through a toolchain in a staging environment.

Next steps (for me)
- Quick spike: draft the JSON schema and a canonical example for 3 use-cases (faq, code-assist, onramp-normalizer). Target 2 days.
- Sync with Mira (infra) on sandbox options and Ravi (console) about telemetry surface.
- Add a stubbed console mockup (screenshot-level) and collect 3 internal devs to try prototyping a chain.

Notes to self / heuristics
- Keep the UX metaphor: "toy pipeline" not "workflow engine". That will keep expectations sane.
- Expose cost tradeoffs early in the editor as the single most important decision point.
- Treat hosted fallback as a safety valve: should never change semantic output, only degrade latency/cost.

[end of jot]
